triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale reads 'This governing infinitive-of-purpose is itself the syntactic continuation of the preceding row's closing motive clause at 6:23' — a positional row reference, barred by the register law (row prose describes the text; cross-row references are verse-anchored). REG TEST 2: the embedded textual claim is byte-TRUE, so this scores low rather than medium. oshb:Prov.6.23 opens on the motive particle כִּ֤י (byte tier) and oshb:Prov.6.24 opens on the lamed-prefixed infinitive construct לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ (byte tier), a grammatically dependent purpose clause; stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap across the 6:23|6:24 seam is 0 tokens, so nothing in the bytes contradicts the continuity claim itself. The defect is the register, not the fact.

findings.claim: The row's opening seam at 6:23/6:24 carries neither of the two seam signals the book rules for C1 and is conceded by the row itself to cut a syntactically continuous construction, while the tier-3-corroborated rival is rejected circularly.
findings.grounds: oshb:Prov.6.24 opens on לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ (byte tier), a lamed-infinitive construct of purpose that must depend on a preceding finite clause — here the כִּ֤י motive clause of oshb:Prov.6.23 (byte tier); the row states this itself and adds that the seam 'lacks a vocative-restart of its own'. Neither ruled C1 seam signal stands at 6:24: the word-bound bni vocative spine in ch 6 sits at 6:1, 6:3 and 6:20 (the toolkit's E-1-corrected 22-verse list), not at 6:24; and the WLC parashah layer marks Prov.6.5, Prov.6.11, Prov.6.15, Prov.6.19, Prov.6.26 and Prov.6.35 in this chapter (pmarks_Prov.json, PE, single-witness) — quoted as an inventory fact, not as counterevidence by absence. There is no positive continuity device either: stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap 6:23|6:24 = 0, so the seam rests on topic shift alone in a row that simultaneously argues syntactic continuity across it. The one rival the row does name — a 6:20-26 / 6:27-35 re-cut corroborated by the PE at oshb:Prov.6.26 (tier-3, single-witness) — is rejected on the strength of the same 6:24 infinitive the row concedes is dependent on 6:23, which is circular. The rationale also enlists the parashah layer's silence at the seam, which the book's own tier rule bars from carrying argumentative weight in either direction.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY, routes onward. Seam-pair cure = one edit: move the M8-Prov-026 / M8-Prov-027 seam from 6:23/6:24 to 6:26/6:27, giving M8-Prov-026 = Prov.6.20-Prov.6.26 and M8-Prov-027 = Prov.6.27-Prov.6.29, so no row splits the 6:23 -> 6:24 purpose construction and both units sit inside the ~4-8 verse C1 range. The replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original: argue 6:26/6:27 from the text (the causal ki-clause warrant of 6:26 closing before the paired rhetorical questions of 6:27-28 open), with the PE at oshb:Prov.6.26 named only as tier-3 single-witness corroboration. Live alternative: merge the two rows into one vocative-anchored lecture Prov.6.20-Prov.6.29. Either route re-opens observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence on both rows.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale references a neighbouring decision positionally rather than by verse anchor.

The register law admits verse-anchored cross-references only; the underlying fact (the lamed-infinitive לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ, oshb:Prov.6.24, byte tier, continues the כִּ֤י clause of oshb:Prov.6.23, byte tier) is byte-true and can be stated without the row reference.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: rewrite as a verse-anchored statement, e.g. 'the governing infinitive of oshb:Prov.6.24 continues the motive clause of oshb:Prov.6.23'.

findings.claim: The petuchah at Prov.6.19 is argued in prose but listed as a bare ref without the mark/witness qualifier the sibling entry carries.

triggers.grounds: boundary_rationale closes 'before the next lecture reopens at 7:1 outside this part' — a writer-part (work-unit) reference, barred by the register law. REG TEST 2: the claim it carries is byte-true, so this scores low. oshb:Prov.7.1 opens the word-bound bni vocative (one of the toolkit's E-1-corrected 22 verses), stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap 6:35|7:1 = 0, and the mark cited at the closing edge is right: pmarks_Prov.json records Prov.6.35 as PE (WLC, single witness), disclosed as tier-3 corroboration in device_notes and qualified in the refs list.

findings.grounds: 'outside this part' names a work unit, not a text unit; the strategy's part plan is a tiling of labour, and 7:1 stands in the same collection parent (C1 Prov.1.1-Prov.9.18) as this row. findings.claim: Neither rejected alternative is the strongest live rival for this span, and the rival disclosed by the adjoining row at the shared 6:26 petuchah is not weighed.
findings.grounds: The field rejects single_proverb and numerical_saying. single_proverb is the ruled default of C2 and C5, not of C1, where this row sits (parent C1 Prov.1.1-Prov.9.18); and the chapter's numerical saying stands at Prov.6.16-Prov.6.19 (the six/seven x-of-y opener at oshb:Prov.6.16), outside this span, so neither rival was ever live. The live rival is the one the adjoining row states and rejects: a 6:20-26 / 6:27-35 re-cut corroborated by the PE at oshb:Prov.6.26 (pmarks_Prov.json, tier-3, single-witness), which would move this row's opening edge from 6:30 to 6:27.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: replace the field's rivals with the 6:27-6:35 re-cut and reject it (or accept it) from the bytes — the subject shift at oshb:Prov.6.30 to the thief, against the tier-3 mark at oshb:Prov.6.26. Field repair only; the span proposal for this seam-pair is recorded on M8-Prov-027.

triggers.grounds: The band is calibrated. The book's low-confidence policy names 'catchword-cluster rows whose cohesion evidence is thinner than 2 shared content tokens' as an expected low-confidence region, and this pair is exactly that: the forms are בְּרָכָ֥ה (oshb:Prov.11.25, byte tier) and וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.11.26, byte tier), so the stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap of the pair is 0 exact tokens and the tie is a skeleton-substring recurrence of ברכה — which the row states as a substring sweep and whose non-uniform word-forms the row discloses verbatim (bare at 11:25, prefixed at 10:7 and 11:26). The cited digit is right: sweep.py --skel returns 3 verses (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26) and the disclosed construct set is right too (3 verses: Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25). The edges are clean (overlap 11:24|11:25 = 0 and 11:26|11:27 = 0), the rival's rejection is byte-true (neither 11:24 nor 11:27 carries the noun), frontier_flag_considered is true, and device_notes gives a bespoke reason for holding the band (two different parallelism types under one shared noun). Neither over- nor under-stated.

findings.class: E-05 count-object discipline / incomplete set disclosure
findings.claim: The rival's rejection leans on 'the noun's rarity' — a lexeme-level claim — while the only digit given is a 3-verse figure for one spelling and the disclosed 'different spelling' set omits the plural, which contains the closest parallel to the row's own cited form.
findings.grounds: Re-swept with the object named (sweep.py --skel, verse counts): ברכה = 3 verses (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26) — the row's digit and set are correct; ברכת = 3 verses (Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25) — the construct set the row does disclose; but ברכות = 2 further verses (Prov.10.6, Prov.28.20), undisclosed, and the bare string ברכ stands in 8 verses book-wide. The omitted set holds the nearest parallel to this row's own evidence: Prov.10.6 places בְּ֭רָכוֹת (oshb:Prov.10.6, byte tier) on לְרֹ֣אשׁ (oshb:Prov.10.6, byte tier) exactly as Prov.11.26 places וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.11.26, byte tier) on לְרֹ֣אשׁ (oshb:Prov.11.26, byte tier). With 8 verses carrying the root string and a same-construction sibling at Prov.10.6, 'the noun's rarity' is not supported by the cited 3, and the disclosure that names one omitted spelling set while omitting another reads as complete when it is not.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: either add the plural set and the root-string digit (ברכות = 2 verses, Prov.10.6 and Prov.28.20; ברכ = 8 verses book-wide) to the disclosure, or drop the rarity leg and rest the cluster on the adjacency of the two hits plus the shared giving/withholding-and-reward pattern, which the row already argues.

findings.claim: An observed_substrate_signals sentence misidentifies which two of the three sweep hits are adjacent.
findings.grounds: The line enumerates 'bare form at Prov.11.25, prefixed forms at Prov.10.7 and Prov.11.26 — the latter two of these three sites sit adjacent'. The latter two named are Prov.10.7 and Prov.11.26, which are not adjacent (they are 19 verses and a chapter apart); the adjacent pair is Prov.11.25|Prov.11.26, as the boundary_rationale itself states ('this pair alone stands adjacent among them'). At best the sentence is ambiguous between enumeration order and book order in a field that must be exact.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: name the adjacent pair explicitly (Prov.11.25 and Prov.11.26) instead of 'the latter two'.

triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative closes 'and the part's own tiling ends at this verse', and the rationale carries a second work-unit reference, 'belongs to this verse by itself in the part' — both barred by the register law. REG TEST 2: the workflow fact is true (the strategy tiles P05 as 9:1-11:31) but it is not re-derivable from bytes and it stands where a text warrant for the forward edge belongs; the edge is independently byte-sound, so the defect is register, scored low. Stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap Prov.11.31|Prov.12.1 = 0 tokens, and the a-fortiori particles הֵ֣ן ... אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי (oshb:Prov.11.31, byte tier) do open this verse and no other in the book as a pair.

findings.class: E-06 register bleed / E-18 workflow warrant
findings.claim: The forward-edge reason given is a writer-part tiling fact rather than a text fact, and the rationale scopes its construction claim to the same work unit.
findings.grounds: 'the part's own tiling ends at this verse' names a unit of labour; a part boundary is not a text boundary and cannot be re-derived from bytes. The rationale's 'belongs to this verse by itself in the part' scopes the same way.

findings.claim: Two frequency claims — one exclusivity, one dismissal of the row's only real shared token — carry no digit-bearing sweep citation.
findings.grounds: (a) 'belongs to this verse by itself in the part' is an exclusivity claim with no digit and a work-unit scope. Re-swept with the object named (sweep.py --skel, verse counts): אף כי stands in 6 verses book-wide (Prov.11.31, Prov.15.11, Prov.17.7, Prov.19.7, Prov.19.10, Prov.21.27) and הן in 2 (Prov.11.31, Prov.24.12), so the pairing of the two particles is confined to 1 verse book-wide — a stronger and byte-checkable statement than the one written. The dismissal is true, but undigited where the book requires a digit-bearing sweep citation.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: add the swept digits and their objects (particle pair: 1 verse book-wide; צדיק: 66 verses book-wide).

triggers.grounds: Over-stated: the low-band label sits on top of a byte-defective warrant, which is the failure mode the lowband test names. The row's stated reason for the band is that its catchword is 'one content token rather than a construction run' — but the two forms are וּלְשׁ֖וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.18, word 5 of 7, byte tier) and לְשׁ֣וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.19, word 7 of 8, byte tier), which are unequal at byte, accent_stripped AND skeleton tier (skeleton forms ולשון and לשון), so the pair shares 0 stoplist-filtered skeleton content tokens. Matching finding recorded at high severity.

findings.claim: The cluster's sole cohesion warrant — an 'exact same noun ... byte tier' repetition, restated in observed_substrate_signals as an 'exact skeleton token ... repeated' — is byte-false at both tiers it names, leaving the C2 atomic default live.
findings.grounds: The two forms are וּלְשׁ֖וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.18, word 5 of 7, byte tier) and לְשׁ֣וֹן (oshb:Prov.12.19, word 7 of 8, byte tier). Programmatic comparison at the staged tiers: byte-equal False, accent_stripped-equal False, skeleton-equal False — the skeleton forms are ולשון and לשון, differing by the conjunction. Sweeps (sweep.py --skel, verse counts): the exact skeleton token ולשון stands in 3 verses (Prov.10.31, Prov.12.18, Prov.25.15), while the contiguous skeleton substring לשון stands in 16 verses — two different count objects, neither named. By the campaign's own stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token metric the pair Prov.12.18|Prov.12.19 shares 0 tokens, so the merge's evidence scores zero on the measure the cluster bar uses, and the ruled C2 default (two single_proverb rows) is live. The real tie is lexeme-level only, and the row nowhere discloses the conjunction prefix that breaks the identity — the sibling cluster row at Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 makes exactly that disclosure for its own prefixed form, so the standard was available inside the same corpus.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY, routes onward. Restate the warrant at lexeme tier, disclosing that Prov.12.18 carries the waw-prefixed form and Prov.12.19 the bare form, with both digits and objects named (exact token ולשון = 3 verses; skeleton substring לשון = 16 verses). If the adjudicator holds the cluster bar to exact shared content tokens, split the row into the ruled C2 atomics Prov.12.18-Prov.12.18 and Prov.12.19-Prov.12.19. Either route re-opens observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence.

findings.claim: Three positional statements about the tongue-noun are byte-false for Prov.12.18, and the rationale contradicts the row's own device_notes.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'Both verses close on the exact same noun for tongue' — oshb:Prov.12.18 closes on מַרְפֵּֽא and oshb:Prov.12.19 on שָֽׁקֶר (both byte tier); neither verse closes on the noun, as the row's own device_notes concedes ('not verse-final'). device_notes: the noun 'sits as the second-to-last word of its own colon in both verses' — in Prov.12.18 the B-colon runs words 4-6 of 7 and the noun is its FIRST word; the claim holds only for Prov.12.19 (words 6-7 of 8). observed_substrate_signals: 'repeated at the seam between the two verses' — the two occurrences sit at word 5 of 7 and word 7 of 8, so neither is seam-adjacent and the recurrence is not the anadiplosis-style tie the wording implies. check_universals.py over the shipped row independently flags the 'second-to-last' sentence.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: delete the 'close on' and 'at the seam' framings and state the actual positions (Prov.12.18 word 5 of 7, colon-initial; Prov.12.19 word 7 of 8).

findings.claim: The embedded prev row's account of the 12:17/12:18 edge contradicts this row's own (correct) falsehood-root disclosure.

Two adjacent rows therefore argue the same edge incompatibly, and the correct account is this row's.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: field repair on the neighbouring row M8-Prov-112 — narrow 'shares no lexeme' to 'shares no exact content token', since the falsehood lexeme does recur at Prov.12.19.

triggers.grounds: Calibrated, if conservative. The band is set for a genuine lexical crux that the row declares non-load-bearing for the seam, and the book's low-confidence policy expressly sanctions registering crux verses low (its named examples include the dry-morsel homograph zone at Prov.17.1). The seam itself is independently sound: stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap is 0 at both edges (Prov.12.25|Prov.12.26 and Prov.12.26|Prov.12.27), the span uses the full X-X single-verse form, no parashah, paseq or K/Q object touches it (pmarks_Prov.json records no mark and no paseq in ch 12 and its single K/Q note at Prov.12.14), and the WEB run quoted for the crux is verbatim at web:Prov.12.26 (check_web_quotes.py GREEN, 0 flags). frontier_flag_considered is true and the uncertainty text is row-specific. Under-statement is the honest direction here, not a masked defect.

findings.claim: The row's central claim is an original-language claim about a Hebrew verb, yet no Hebrew appears anywhere in the row and no oshb: ref is cited.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reasons about 'The A-colon's opening verb', its root and 'the bare consonants as staged here'; observed_substrate_signals says the root 'is not transparent from the skeleton form alone' — but the form is never shown, the row contains zero Hebrew characters in any field, and boundary_evidence_refs carries only web:Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16 and web:Prov.12.26, with no oshb: ref anywhere in the row, while strong_or_hebrew_tags_used is set true. The form is יָתֵ֣ר (oshb:Prov.12.26, word 0, byte tier; skeleton יתר). The book requires the original language to be quoted for every boundary-relevant original-language claim, and the parallel crux row at Prov.13.23 in the same writer part does quote its disputed noun, so the standard was met elsewhere. As written the crux — which is the sole reason for the confidence band — cannot be checked from the row.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: add the byte-tier splice יָתֵ֣ר with an oshb:Prov.12.26 ref in-field and in boundary_evidence_refs, and name the skeleton form יתר in the observed_substrate_signals line that appeals to it.

triggers.grounds: Calibrated. This is the book's named low-confidence region — a catchword cluster thinner than two shared content tokens — and here the warrant is byte-TRUE: כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.13.19, word 5 of 8, byte tier) and כְסִילִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.13.20, word 7 of 9, byte tier) are skeleton-equal, giving exactly 1 shared stoplist-filtered skeleton content token — the only shared token at any seam of this row (13:18|13:19 = 0 and 13:20|13:21 = 0). The band matches the evidence.

findings.claim: The rationale's Hebrew splice binds to a ketiv/qere verse without a K/Q disclosure in that same field.
findings.grounds: citation_sweep.py over the shipped row returns the warn: 'Hebrew quote in row.boundary_rationale binds to K/Q verse oshb:Prov.13.20 with no ketiv/qere disclosure in-field'. pmarks_Prov.json records 2 K/Q notes at Prov.13.20 (of 69 notes over 63 verses book-wide) and the staged verse carries each unpointed ketiv inline before its pointed qere, which is the inline-ketiv hazard the toolkit names for slicing in K/Q verses. findings.claim: The identity of the two fools-forms is asserted under a byte-tier label but holds only at skeleton tier.
findings.grounds: כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.13.19, byte tier) carries a dagesh in the kaf and כְסִילִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.13.20, byte tier) does not, and their accents differ. findings.class: cross-row equivalence overstates the compared row
findings.claim: The row equates its own byte-true one-token catchword with the Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 pairing, whose token identity does not hold.

For this row that is exact: the skeleton token כסילים is shared and the stoplist-filtered overlap is 1. For Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 the skeleton forms are ולשון and לשון, giving 0 shared content tokens, so the compared pairing does not rest on one repeated token at all. The equivalence imports that row's defective characterisation and makes a true warrant here look like a copy of a false one there.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: drop the cross-row equivalence, or qualify it once the Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 warrant is repaired.

triggers.grounds: Calibrated, if conservative — the same crux logic the book's low-confidence policy sanctions. The disputed noun רָאשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Prov.13.23, word 3 of 8, byte tier) is a genuine crux: the spelling stands in exactly 1 verse in Prov (sweep.py --skel, verse count) and no morphology layer is staged in this extract, so the sense cannot be machine-settled; the row discloses this rather than resolving it and declares it non-load-bearing for the seam. The seam is independently sound: stoplist-filtered skeleton content-token overlap is 0 at both edges (13:22|13:23 and 13:23|13:24), the span uses the full X-X form, and no mark object touches it (pmarks_Prov.json: nearest PE at Prov.13.25, no paseq in ch 13, the chapter's K/Q pair at Prov.13.20). frontier_flag_considered is true and the uncertainty text is row-specific.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals labels the B-colon connector 'waw-adversative' while the row's own rationale and device_notes read the verse as one sustained, non-antithetic thought.
findings.grounds: The B-colon opens on וְיֵ֥שׁ (oshb:Prov.13.23, word 4 of 8, byte tier) — the existential with a simple conjunction, the same construction the single-verse row at Prov.11.24 characterises as existential 'rather than a simple antithetic bicolon'. This row's boundary_rationale says the verse is 'one sustained thought rather than a subject-vs-subject antithesis' and device_notes types it 'Synthetic parallelism', so the oss line is the boilerplate carried by the surrounding antithetic single-proverb rows and contradicts this row's own type call. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of the reading it is supposed to support, and the only English adversative here is the WEB rendering, which is tier-4 and cannot carry the label.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: replace the oss line with the construction actually present (an existential clause opening the B-colon with a plain conjunction at oshb:Prov.13.23).
